title: Percentage Calculation Methodology
overview: Percentage calculations are fundamental to math and everyday life. Understanding the three main percentage problems (finding percentage, finding the whole, finding the part) enables quick mental math and accurate calculations.

methods.name: X% of Y (Find the Part)
methods.description: The most common calculation: finding a percentage of a number. Used for discounts, tips, taxes, and more.

formula.name: Finding X% of Y
formula.expression:
Part = (Percentage / 100) × Whole
Or: Part = Percentage × Whole / 100

methods.name: X is What % of Y (Find the Percentage)
methods.description: Finding what percentage one number is of another. Used for comparisons, statistics, and data analysis.

methods.name: Percentage Change (Increase/Decrease)
methods.description: Calculating the percentage difference between two values. Essential for tracking growth, inflation, and performance.

formula.name: Percentage Change
formula.expression:
% Change = ((New - Old) / Old) × 100

Positive = Increase
Negative = Decrease

limitations: Division by zero if old value is 0
Not symmetric (50% increase ≠ 50% decrease to return)

methods.name: Reverse Percentage (Find Original)
methods.description: Finding the original value before a percentage increase or decrease was applied.

formula.name: Reverse Calculation
formula.expression:
For increase: Original = Final / (1 + %/100)
For decrease: Original = Final / (1 - %/100)
formula.description: Example: Price after 20% off is $80. Original = $80 / 0.8 = $100

footnotes: Per cent means 'per hundred' (Latin: per centum)
100% increase doubles a value; 50% decrease halves it
Percentage points ≠ percent (5% to 6% is 1 percentage point but 20% increase)
Quick mental math: 10% = divide by 10, 5% = half of 10%, 1% = divide by 100
disclaimer: Percentage calculations assume accurate input values. For financial decisions, verify calculations independently.
